goal: Measure the actual owned native context authorization path without altering selected readers, original fixture, model boundaries, budgets or callback protocols.
procedure: Read original executor, native context authorization and existing aggregate observers first. Run the unchanged selected native comparison case in an optional fresh diagnostic process. Install a parent hook and future-thread dispatcher only after refusing occupied hooks/monitoring; classify exact original SelectedNativeReadServices._read work code. Record bounded numeric ledgers per thread with fixed approved synchronous tags and own-thread CPU samples. Keep windows separate from tagged totals and report overlap/untagged limits. Apply the bounded parent-only diagnostic cap only at a new outer RPC with no active observed RPC or classified owned work, never in a worker. On close stop recording, restore only unchanged owned parent/future hooks, and let survivors remove only the inert dispatcher on their next Python event. Do not cancel, wait for or alter workers. Persist output suppression through normal interpreter exit and emit only aggregate hashes/counters and fixed status. Validate lifecycle/privacy mechanics with ordinary controlled threads; actual selected-engine observation remains pending.
authority: The observer supplies no authorization, model output, qualification or publication evidence. Exact original current permissions, owned connections, runtime lineage and unchanged fixture/runtime cleanup remain authoritative.
validation: Sixteen focused ordinary-thread lifecycle/privacy checks passed before freeze. They verify separate stacks and numeric windows, occupied current/future/monitoring refusal, preserved hook replacements, deferred idle/active-survivor self-removal, no post-close recording, bounded ledger/stack state, parent cap deferral while owned CPU-only work is active, absence of worker cap exceptions, numeric privacy and suppression of late Python/native output through normal process exit. These checks do not substitute for the original integration case or qualify actual engine behavior/latency. The workflow and CLI default to a 180-second parent-only cap, and the CLI rejects caps above 180 seconds; original 60000ms response/read settings remain unchanged. Actual exact-head aggregate receipt is pending.
failure_or_lesson: A parent-only clock cannot attribute work in an owned reader thread. Sharing a stack or sampling another thread CPU clock gives false attribution. Future-thread inheritance restoration does not remove existing per-thread hooks; safe close needs an inert dispatcher with deferred self-removal, incomplete last-sample spans and preserved later replacements. A cap must not provoke cleanup while an owned read is still executing, and late output suppression must outlive the driver without force-stopping workers.
